newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: DAINONG ASKS FOR URGENT HELP FROM PRIME BANK - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: DAINONG ASKS FOR URGENT HELP FROM PRIME BANK - PAPER.

text.p: South Korea's troubled Dainong Group has asked its prime bank, SEOULBANK, for urgent financial help, a leading business newspaper said on Wednesday.
A senior Dainong official confirmed the group's chairman had visited SEOULBANK on Tuesday. But he refused to comment on the other details in the newspaper report.

"Chairman Park Yong-hak visited SEOULBANK on the occasion of the inauguration of the bank's new president," said the official in Dainong's planning office, who declined to be identified. "But I cannot confirm whether he asked for urgent help."
The Maeil Business Newspaper said Park had asked the bank to extend financial help to keep his group's core units alive.
Four Dainong affiliates, including Dainong Corp and Midopa Department Store, have been put under protection by banks from defaulting on debt payments.
The two-month protection period for Dainong was due to expire in two weeks, the report said.

Maeil reported that Park had been alarmed by an interim report from an accounting firm, commissioned by creditor banks to assess management of the four firms, that presented a negative opinion on the future of the companies.
The Dainong official said the accounting firm's final report was expected to be submitted next week both to the creditor banks and the group's top management.
The assessment results were expected to strongly influence creditors when they discuss the future of the group's four units after the protection period ended.
